exposure: Embryo quality (poor-quality blastocyst vs. good-quality blastocyst)
outcome: Placental findings (anatomic, inflammatory, vascular malperfusion, villous maturation lesions)
cohort: Live singleton births after IVF with a single blastocyst transfer at a university-affiliated tertiary hospital between 2009 and 2017 were included.
finding: Transfer of poor-quality embryos was associated with a higher rate of low-lying placentas and several adverse placental lesions, including villitis of unknown etiology, distal villous hypoplasia, intervillous thrombosis, multiple maternal malperfusion lesions, and parenchymal calcifications.
